answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. In effect, the network makes cheating the most expensive strategy available, which is the closest thing to a Sybil-resistant design that economics allows. Consider a ivory as the anchor of the cost. A knoll stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a haven holds the rep...
